name: Why did the tutor say 'no problem'?
rule: Pick the ONE code that best explains why a reasonable reader would say this passage shows no current problem. If two fit, take the one higher in this list.

codes.label: Already resolved
codes.definition: The passage describes a problem the team has fixed or is handling successfully.
codes.example: After last week's issue we split the backend tasks more evenly.

codes.label: Future or hypothetical
codes.definition: A plan, intention, worry or guess. Nothing has gone wrong yet.
codes.example: We need to make sure we communicate better next time.

codes.label: Normal setback
codes.definition: Something went wrong with the work (delay, bug, changed plan) but nothing broke down between people.
codes.example: Our deployment took longer than we planned.

codes.label: Real but minor
codes.definition: A genuine people or workload issue, but small enough that a tutor would not act on it.
codes.example: One member was a bit quiet in Monday's meeting.

codes.label: Nothing there
codes.definition: The passage does not describe a problem at all (neutral or positive).
codes.example: I worked on the login page this week.

codes.label: Genuine problem
codes.definition: In your reading the passage shows a real, current problem (of any kind) that a tutor should know about; the tutor's 'None' looks like a miss. Say which kind in the note.
codes.example: Two of us did almost all the work again this fortnight and nobody has said anything.

codes.label: Other
codes.definition: None of the above. Write a short note saying why.
